title: The Tale of Two Brothers
text:
Two brothers lived together in ancient Egypt. Anpu, the elder, had a house and a wife. Bata, the younger, lived with them and worked the fields and the cattle, and the story says there was no one as strong in all the land.

One day Anpu's wife tried to seduce Bata. He refused, angry, and promised to say nothing of it. But she, afraid, made herself look as if she had been beaten and told her husband that Bata had attacked her. Anpu sharpened his spear and hid behind the stable door to kill his brother when he came home.

The cows warned Bata. He fled, and the sun god placed a stretch of water full of crocodiles between the brothers. Across it, Bata told Anpu the truth and swore a terrible oath of innocence. Anpu believed him and wept, but Bata would not come back. He went to the distant Valley of the Cedar, telling Anpu that if his beer ever foamed, it would mean Bata was in danger. Anpu went home and killed his wife.

Years later Anpu's beer foamed. He set out at once, searched for years, found his brother's heart and brought him back to life. In the end Bata became king of Egypt, and Anpu succeeded him.
lesson: A false accusation inside a family can do damage that takes years to repair. Listen to both sides before acting in anger, and be ready to do hard work to make it right.
source: The Tale of Two Brothers, Papyrus D'Orbiney (British Museum EA 10183), 19th Dynasty
